# Consistent Planner snapshot

`POST /internal/v1/students/{studentID}/learning-paths/{pathID}/planning-snapshot`
returns `student-planning-snapshot.v1` for one exact Student-owned path. It uses
the existing dedicated `LEARNING_PLANNER_INTERNAL_TOKEN`. An absent Planner
token leaves the route unregistered. The general internal credential does not
grant access. Shared-token authentication remains the existing trust boundary;
this endpoint adds no JWT verification or public/browser route.

The response implements the coherent Student-owned input projection for T20.1 under the
[accepted Hybrid Replanning ADR](https://github.com/bemulima/ms-go-learning-planner/blob/main/docs/hybrid-mastery-replanning.md).
Student owns the observation; Planner owns planning significance and evaluation.
This read neither evaluates a plan nor grants permission to apply one.

## Request

```json
{
  "targets": [{"type": "concept", "key": "go.syntax", "version": "v1"}],
  "trigger_context": {
    "kind": "manual_request",
    "reason": "Inspect the current owner state",
    "correlation_id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
  }
}
```

There must be 1–500 unique exact `concept`/`capability` references. The existing
opaque key and version envelope is retained: key up to 255 bytes, optional
version up to 128 bytes. An empty version identifies the exact legacy
unversioned projection. Student never derives a graph version, and this
compatibility identity makes no qualified Hybrid-target policy claim.

`kind` and `reason` are required nonblank UTF-8 caller trace. They have no new
planning vocabulary or policy interpretation. If present, `correlation_id` must
be a canonical nonzero UUID. Trace is carried separately from applicability
references; it is not authoritative evidence, consent, or a significance
classification.

The body requires `application/json` and is capped at 2 MiB. URL IDs must be
canonical nonzero UUIDs. Duplicate keys, nulls anywhere, unknown or differently
cased field names, duplicate targets, trailing values, and malformed/oversize
input fail before the owner read. These are technical wire bounds, not numerical
planning-policy parameters.

## Observation and references

One repeatable-read, read-only PostgreSQL transaction reads the exact owned
path, selected context, onboarding profile, ordered requested mastery,
normalized safe evidence-reference metadata, frozen requirements and activity
fact references, and local Course/Practice action bindings. Missing mastery
uses the existing `UNKNOWN` projection without inserting a row. The read makes
no sibling HTTP calls and writes no receipt, event, counter, or aggregate.

The explicit response whitelist contains:

- `schema`, learner/path identity, `captured_at`, caller `trigger_context` and the
  normalized `requested_targets`;
- `references`: content-addressed `learner_ref`, `mastery_ref`, `goal_ref`,
  `constraints_ref`, and complete `snapshot_ref`;
- `profile`: declared codes, stack preferences, language, pace/time constraints
  and existing `owner_version`;
- `path`: exact Course/path identity, existing `path_version` and
  `journey_version`, selection, ordered item identities/statuses, exact lesson
  revisions, frozen requirements and their satisfaction;
- requested `mastery`, safe `evidence` references, `activity_facts`, and
  Student-known `course_bindings`/`practice_bindings` preserving action and
  TaskInstance associations; evidence references retain frozen evidence class,
  official outcome, normalized support/evidence kind, and the persisted Practice
  `surface_classification` when present;
- explicit capability and policy `availability`.

Hashes bind the canonical typed, sorted relevant projection and exact requested
target set. Capture time and caller trace do not change applicability by
themselves. Existing profile version conservatively anchors goal and constraints,
including an owner version change after an ABA update. These references are
content addresses plus existing coarse owner versions; they are not newly
persisted independent monotonic learner/mastery/goal counters. Current path and
journey counters keep their existing meaning.

Protected `COMPLETED`/`IN_PROGRESS` item identities, revisions, requirements,
satisfaction, successful fact references, and local execution associations are
retained. Local bindings do not assert a remote Runtime hold, safe checkpoint,
or lifecycle state that Student does not own.

Lesson prose, goal/reason prose, answer or solution bodies, raw evidence,
workspace, prompts, credentials, private evaluation assets and sibling Runtime
projections have no response fields. Output is validated and marshaled completely
before sending, with a 128 MiB whole-payload technical cap. Oversize fails closed
without truncating protected state or adding smaller per-item semantic limits.
Responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## Planner-owned Hybrid Policy V1 inputs

`evidence_quality` and `stability` report `status: "DERIVED_BY_PLANNER"`,
`value: null`, and `reason_code: "PLANNER_POLICY_HYBRID_V1"`. The accepted
Operational Hybrid Policy V1 belongs to Planner. Student supplies committed
objective provenance and current mastery without classifying planning quality,
stability, significance, or automatic permission.

Complete evidence references for the exact requested target identities include
`source_kind`, frozen `evidence_class`, official `outcome`, normalized `kind`,
assistance support and hints, exact task/TaskInstance identities, and immutable
receipt references. For v2 Practice the projection reads `surface_classification`
from the persisted action, including detached closed history, rather than
inferring it from the current path. Known values are `practice` and `project`.
An absent surface stays absent so Planner can return UNKNOWN when provenance
cannot establish a quality class. Malformed source identities, assistance,
receipt joins, or surface values fail closed.

Planner can count `independent_application` evidence and distinct identities
using the same task identity as the existing Student reducer: Course `task_id`
and Practice `task_instance_id`. Independent knowledge-check successes remain
separate. Student does not alter mastery mathematics, the cumulative reducer,
or confidence (`evidence_count / (evidence_count + 2)`).

`runtime_hold`, `automatic_adaptation`, and `student_pinning` remain
`status: "UNAVAILABLE"`, `value: null`, with explicit machine reasons. A read
provides no consent and invents no Runtime hold. Trigger sequencing/coalescing,
Planner evaluation, and Student application remain later sequential cards.

## Errors and verification

Malformed input returns 400; owner validation returns 422. Missing and foreign
ownership both return 404. Inconsistent state returns 409, owner/storage or
malformed/oversize output returns 500, and a missing configured getter returns
503. Responses contain safe machine codes rather than provider errors.

The declared `planning_snapshot_read_integration` command is the isolated
registered HTTP/PG proof, gated by `STUDENT_PLANNING_SNAPSHOT_PROOF=1` and
`STUDENT_PLANNING_SNAPSHOT_TEST_DATABASE_URL`. Root prepares the new exact
`remediation_t201_student_integration_proof` database at `127.0.0.1:58998 or native 58999` with
current owner migrations, then runs the file-only test. Workers do not
start services or migrate databases. The registered HTTP/PG proof names its retained owner metadata fixtures,
including execution/project/assessment provenance. It proves read-only
projection and concurrent consistency, and makes no Runtime evidence-ingress
or full-E2E claim. Quality/stability derivation is tested in Planner.
